proxyPrefixes.networkHelp: Only change the network if this proxy looks at the SAME network as another. Two identical ranges attached to the same network merge what both proxies discover; attached to distinct networks, they stay separate. When in doubt, leave the network specific to the proxy: wrongly separating costs a duplicate, wrongly merging melts two devices into a single sheet.

discover.scanHelp1: The scan probes administration ports, reads the SSH banner and the web header, then tries the instance's discovery credentials — over SSH, and on the web interface of devices that require it.
discover.scanHelp2: Identification therefore relies on what the device exposes: SSH banner, header and title of its web page, and — if a standard credential works — the output of its version command.

lldp.viaPortId: recognized by the hardware address of one of its ports
lldp.viaSysName: recognized by its system name only — least certain match
lldp.multipleNeighborsNote: {{count}} neighbors on this single port: LLDP frames are probably crossing a switch that doesn't consume them. None of these neighbors is therefore necessarily at the end of the cable.
lldp.observedBothSides: observed, and both devices see each other
lldp.observedOneSide: observed from one side only — this is the ORDINARY case: the device on the other end may not speak LLDP (MikroTik on SwOS don't), or meshcraft couldn't name the remote port on its facade
lldp.observedUnplaced: observed, but the neighbor is on no device of this site: it's not known where to place the other end
lldp.silencePlatformUnsupported: LLDP neighborhood UNKNOWN, and it will stay that way: this platform doesn't speak LLDP. Its ports may be cabled without meshcraft being able to tell — at best a neighbor will see it, it will see no one. This isn't a meshcraft shortcoming, no version will change anything about it.
lldp.silenceNotServed: LLDP neighborhood UNKNOWN: this device was indeed queried and publishes no neighbor table. Either LLDP is disabled on it, or meshcraft is wrong about what its platform can do — either way, its ports may be cabled without meshcraft being able to tell.
lldp.silenceNeverPolled: LLDP neighborhood UNKNOWN: no reading has arrived yet for this device, even though its platform can provide one. It's missing an SNMP collector, or the first cycle hasn't run yet — that one can be fixed.

portsPage.helpLabel: Help — where the columns come from
portsPage.help1: The "Neighbor" column first shows the OBSERVED LLDP neighborhood — what the device actually sees facing it — and falls back to the DECLARED topology when there's no observation. The cell always states which of the two it shows: LLDP is a dated observation, entered is a human declaration.
portsPage.help2: A port with no neighbor isn't a port with no cable: an entire platform in the fleet may not speak 802.1AB (SwOS), a device may only run LLDP on a few interfaces, and a silent neighbor stays silent.
portsPage.help3: Traffic is MEASURED: it comes from interface counters read via SNMP, derived into a rate by the controller.

serialAdd.equipmentCisco2960xDetail: Catalyst 2960 / 2960-X (IOS) — soft reset via write erase + vlan.dat (9600 8N1). Command set documented, not yet captured on hardware.

Soft reset boots Factory_Default_Config.cfg, deletes startup1.cfg, restarts, then pushes the instance discovery user/password onto the switch (this REPLACES factory admin/admin), applies the site management plan, and probes until the device answers.
serialAdd.instanceCredHelp: After factory reset, meshcraft sets this local user on the switch (username + secret from discovery credentials). If the username is admin, factory admin/admin is overwritten — use this secret for the next serial login. The secret is materialized only for the serial session.

manualIp.subtitle: real connection to the device, then adoption
manualIp.credHelp1: A one-off credential is only used for this attempt: it isn't saved, and it's presented to both SSH and the web interface — you don't have to guess which way meshcraft will get in. To stop retyping it, save it under Configuration → Instance → Discovery credentials.
manualIp.credHelp2: The instance's discovery credentials are also set there: they're tried in priority order, and nothing needs to be retyped here.
manualIp.credHelp3: Attempts stop after two authentication refusals, to avoid locking an account.
manualIp.credHelp4: The details of saved credentials are reserved to instance admins: the controller tries them without them passing through your browser.
manualIp.passwordLabel: Password (an empty password is a value)

scanPrefixes.subtitle: IPv4/IPv6 prefixes declared per proxy
scanPrefixes.domainCreated: Network "{{name}}" created — attach your ranges to it
scanPrefixes.prefixHelp: Assumed limits: at most 4,096 addresses per range (a /20 in IPv4), and in IPv6 nothing wider than a /112 — a /64 contains 1.8·10¹⁹ addresses, it cannot be enumerated. For a single IPv6 device, use manual IP add instead.
scanPrefixes.domainHelp: The network is what gives an address its meaning. Two ranges attached to the same network describe the same LAN: a silent device seen by both proxies counts only once. Attached to two networks, they remain foreign to each other — as with two branch offices both on 192.168.1.0/24. A serial number or MAC address always overrides this classification: they identify the device everywhere.
scanPrefixes.collisionWarning: {{prefix}} is already declared on {{list}}. If this is the SAME network reached via another path, choose its network above: the two proxies' discoveries will merge. If these are two different networks that share this addressing scheme, leave "network specific to this proxy".
scanPrefixes.sharedTitle: This range is declared on several proxies: the network next to it says whether it's the same LAN.

devices.tagWhyPwpolicy: Set by administration password provisioning: this platform's policy doesn't accept the site's secret (maximum length, minimum length, punctuation), and this tag decides which suitable password it receives.
devices.tagWhyDefault: Set by meshcraft based on what this platform's connector declares. It decides an identifier the device receives.

mgmtPlanPage.title: Site management
mgmtPlanPage.subtitle: How devices on this site are administered — VLAN, addressing, gateway
mgmtPlanPage.notConfigured: This site has no explicit plan yet: values below are the cautious default — native VLAN 1, addressing left to network DHCP, meshcraft touches nothing.
mgmtPlanPage.adminVlanHelp1: In native mode, administration uses the port's untagged VLAN: no management VLAN is pushed. Some entry-level devices only accept this.
mgmtPlanPage.adminVlanHelp2: Some devices only accept admin on native VLAN, or only VLAN 1. Adopting them in a tagged plan would make them unreachable — meshcraft refuses adoption and explains why.
mgmtPlanPage.untaggedHint: Admin traffic is not tagged: there is no management VLAN to choose.
mgmtPlanPage.externalDhcpNote: meshcraft configures the device as DHCP client and allocates nothing. The obtained address is observed, not decided — a stable DHCP reservation is still recommended.
mgmtPlanPage.meshcraftManagedNote: meshcraft picks a free address in the range below and pushes static configuration. meshcraft is not a DHCP server — it keeps the address inventory.
mgmtPlanPage.conformityHelp: Unchecked, a non-conforming device can be adopted keeping its current addressing: it stays administrable but appears off-plan with reason. Checked, adoption is refused — strictest policy.
mgmtPlanPage.strictPlan: Refuse adoption of a device unable to carry this plan (recommended)
mgmtPlanPage.saveNote: Changing this plan does not reconfigure anything by itself: affected devices will show a drift to deploy.

mgmtMigrate.persistTitle: Commit to flash; refused if device does not already declare plan VLAN
mgmtMigrate.prepareBlockedTitle: Refused: no active uplink carries the target management VLAN — switching would cut access.
mgmtMigrate.prepareTitle: Add a DHCP interface on target VLAN without removing anything
mgmtMigrate.step1Help: A closed port is good news: refused proves the packet arrived. Silence is inconclusive. Aim for the gateway — the only address whose existence is guaranteed.
mgmtMigrate.step1Title: 1 · Preflight: can the proxy reach the target network?
mgmtMigrate.step2Help: Adds a DHCP client interface on VLAN {{vlan}} without removing anything: the device keeps its current address. If a lease arrives, a DHCP server responds on this VLAN. Nothing is saved to flash.
mgmtMigrate.step2Title: 2 · Dry run — prove the target network responds
mgmtMigrate.step3Help: Removes the dry-run interface — the device refuses a management VLAN that already has IP — then moves admin to VLAN {{vlan}}. The device drops the current session: no response here is normal. Still nothing in flash.
mgmtMigrate.step4Help: Save to flash. Only after the device responds on its new address: until then a power loss rolls back — your safety net. After this, the net becomes a trap.

discoveryCredsPage.label: Label
discoveryCredsPage.noCredentials: No credentials. Without them, discovery only uses what devices expose without authentication.
discoveryCredsPage.passwordHelp: An empty password is a value, not an omission: it is the factory default on some product lines.
discoveryCredsPage.subtitle: credentials to connect to a device meshcraft does not manage yet
discoveryCredsPage.title: Discovery credentials
discoveryCredsPage.help1: These credentials belong to the instance, not a site: discovery happens before a device has a site. They are tried in priority order during discovery.
discoveryCredsPage.help2: Attempts stop after two authentication failures on the same device, SSH and web combined — to avoid AAA lockouts.
discoveryCredsPage.webAuthHelp1: On the web interface, meshcraft can only present HTTP-level authentication announced by a 401.
discoveryCredsPage.webAuthHelp2: A login form (field + button + cookie session) is not tested this way — that requires a connector.
discoveryCredsPage.secretsUndecryptable: {{count}} secret(s) can no longer be decrypted
discoveryCredsPage.undecryptableNote: with the current encryption key — affected rows are marked below. Re-enter the password on the line.
discoveryCredsPage.keyInDbWarning: The encryption key is stored in the database
discoveryCredsPage.keyInDbDetail: next to the secrets it protects: set MESHCRAFT_SECRET_KEY (64 hex chars) to keep the key off-database.

siteCredsPage.generationCreatedToast: New generation created — previous still valid
siteCredsPage.help1: One credential per site, plus one per device group when password policies differ between models.
siteCredsPage.help2: Revealing a password is logged with your identity.
siteCredsPage.help3: Password policies. Some ranges reject the site secret: MikroTik SwOS caps passwords at 15 characters, and its connector refuses the site secret before sending. meshcraft then generates a suitable password under a technical tag pwpolicy-len<N>, and tags affected devices. These credentials are held by meshcraft: their secret can be revealed and rotated, but scope cannot be changed or deleted.
siteCredsPage.help4: SNMP. An v2c community applies site-wide — read-only: meshcraft never deploys write communities. A v3 identity targets tag snmpv3-<auth>-<priv>. Mixed fleets need as many v3 credentials as cryptographic families.
siteCredsPage.help5: An v3 identity carries two distinct secret phrases: one authenticates, one encrypts. One compromised device in the family exposes monitoring for the whole family.
siteCredsPage.instanceDisabled: Disabled for discovery — still the password on every device it was applied to.
siteCredsPage.instanceIntro: Standard credentials used by discovery — and placed by the serial soft-reset, because the browser has to type a secret on a console the controller cannot open. Equipment provisioned over serial but not yet adopted is reachable only with one of these, not with the site password.
siteCredsPage.keyInDbError: The encryption key is stored in the database it protects (MESHCRAFT_SECRET_KEY missing). A dump leak would expose these passwords.
siteCredsPage.managedScopeTitle: Reserved scope: this credential is generated and held by meshcraft based on what the platform connector declares. Its name and scope cannot be changed; deleting it would leave affected devices without an applicable credential.
siteCredsPage.noCredentials: No credentials defined. Without them, meshcraft cannot connect to devices on this site.
siteCredsPage.noDefaultWarning: No default credential: devices outside groups will have none.
siteCredsPage.noPrivPhrase: no encryption phrase — will not be deployed
siteCredsPage.noPrivWarning: Without encryption: polls travel in clear, only origin is authenticated.
siteCredsPage.noteMaxLenPlaceholder: e.g. 32 characters max on this range
siteCredsPage.perDeviceToast: A distinct secret will be generated per device
siteCredsPage.phrasesMustDiffer: The two phrases must be different.
siteCredsPage.pwPolicyNote: only devices whose platform enforces this password length
siteCredsPage.reservedScopeError: Reserved namespace — choose an operational tag or site scope.
siteCredsPage.reservedScopeErrorDetail: « {{tag}} » belongs to a reserved namespace: these credentials are generated and held by meshcraft based on what each platform connector declares. Choose an operational tag or site scope.
siteCredsPage.revealLogged: This reveal was logged to the site journal with your identity.
siteCredsPage.rotateDeployNote: Creating the generation does not push it yet: deployment is per device with verification.
siteCredsPage.rotateNote: The old secret is not deleted: it moves to retiring and stays valid while devices carry it.
siteCredsPage.rotationCreated: New generation created — previous still valid
siteCredsPage.scopeTagHelp: Prefer tag: a device can carry as many as needed, and tagging rules set them automatically. Group is unique per device and is only assigned via site configuration import — kept for existing fleets that use it.
siteCredsPage.secretNeverReread: This page never re-reads secrets: change replaces, empty keeps.
siteCredsPage.subtitle: What meshcraft installs on devices — and what you use to connect to them
siteCredsPage.title: Site credentials
siteCredsPage.v2cReadNote: read community — meshcraft never deploys write communities
siteCredsPage.v2cRotateNote: For a community, a device left behind simply stops answering polls — it does not become unreachable.
siteCredsPage.v3FamilyNote: only devices of this cryptographic family
siteCredsPage.v3FillBothOrNone: Fill both phrases, or neither: they change together.
siteCredsPage.v3PairTogether: An v3 identity is the pair: they renew together.
siteCredsPage.v3RevealHelp: These two phrases are deliberately different: SNMPv3 derives a key from each.
siteCredsPage.v3RevealHelpFull: These two phrases are deliberately different: SNMPv3 derives a key from each by the same calculation. The same phrase on both sides would make the encryption key only the start of the authentication key — whoever gets one gets the other.
siteCredsPage.v3TargetTagHelp: This identity only applies to devices with this tag: the v3 key derives from the algorithm pair; a device that does not accept them cannot carry it. The tag is technical — provisioning sets it from what the connector announces.

planPage.linkTrafficEmpty: No samples yet for this port.

planPage.lldpEmpty: No LLDP links observed on this site yet.

planPage.linkCapacityNote: Link speed comes from the device (negotiated link). No need to set it here.

profilsPage.title: Port profiles
profilsPage.subtitle: {{count}} profiles · defined by the network engineer
profilsPage.readOnly: Read-only — editing profiles and the VLAN plan is reserved for engineer mode. To apply a profile: switch view, select a port.
profilsPage.vlanPlanEdit: Click a VLAN to rename it or change its color.
profilsPage.vlanPlanReadOnly: Palette and names defined by the network engineer.
profilsPage.stpEnabledHelp: When disabled, the port does not participate in STP/RSTP (SwOS ena, Instant On STP State). RouterOS has no per-port off switch.
profilsPage.bpduGuardHelp: Disables the port if it receives a BPDU (RouterOS bpdu-guard, Instant On CST). Not available on SwOS.

proxyPage.title: Proxies
proxyPage.subtitle: Network presence points of the instance — outbound connection to this controller
proxyPage.noProxies: No proxy enrolled. Deploy one with the docker-compose below.
proxyPage.instanceProxy: Instance proxy — usable by all sites, managed by global admins
proxyPage.pickOneSite: Pick at least one site: a proxy with no coverage would be useless.
proxyPage.tokenHint: Paste on destination instance to migrate, or in MESHCRAFT_ENROLL_TOKEN.
proxyPage.thenComposeUp: Then on proxy host: docker compose up -d
proxyPage.thenSudoInstall: On proxy host: sudo sh meshcraft-proxy-install.sh
proxyPage.autoUpgrade: Automatic upgrade — follow instance build when newer
proxyPage.migrateHint: On destination: Configuration → Proxies → Generate token only. Copy URL and token here.
proxyPage.coverageHelp1: Coverage defines who administers the proxy and for which sites it serves. You only see instance proxies and those covering one of your sites, and you can only add or remove your sites from their coverage. Acting on the proxy itself (revoke, delete, migrate) requires administering all sites it covers.
proxyPage.coverageHelp2: It does not define what the proxy can reach — that is observed. And a discovered device's site is chosen at adoption.
proxyPage.coverageHelp3: Cross-instance migration: first generate an enrollment token on the destination instance, then enter its URL and token here. On its next heartbeat, the proxy enrolls there, rewrites its local state, and switches — nothing to do on the proxy machine.
proxyPage.deployDockerHelp1: The meshcraft/proxy image (amd64, arm64, armv7) is distributed by this controller's built-in registry: generated docker-compose pulls from here and embeds a 1-hour enrollment token.
proxyPage.binaryInstallHelp1: The script detects the host architecture, downloads the matching binary, verifies its SHA-256, creates an unprivileged service account, and installs a hardened systemd unit. It embeds a 1-hour enrollment token and is safe to re-run: an already enrolled identity is not touched.
proxyPage.binaryInstallHelp2: The token is a secret: the script stores it in /etc/meshcraft/proxy.env with mode 0600, never in the systemd unit which is world-readable.
proxyPage.binaryInstallHelp3: Manual start: MESHCRAFT_CONTROLLER (this controller URL) and MESHCRAFT_ENROLL_TOKEN as environment variables. State is persisted in /var/lib/meshcraft/state.json.
proxyPage.renameHelp1: A tracking label, freely editable: the proxy identity is its UUID, not its name. Its enrollment, scan ranges, and access paths are not changed.
proxyPage.coverageModalHelp1: Covered sites determine who sees this proxy, who administers it, and for which sites it can provide access paths.
proxyPage.siteYouAdminTitle: You administer this site: you can remove the proxy from its coverage
proxyPage.siteNotAdminTitle: Covered site you do not administer
proxyPage.upgradeHelp1Full: The proxy downloads its architecture binary, verifies SHA-256, and re-executes. If it does not restart, it falls back to the image binary after two attempts and the failure appears in the table — the Docker image is never touched.
proxyPage.migrateApplyNoteFull: The proxy applies the order on its next heartbeat (≤ 30 s). On failure (unreachable URL, expired token), it stays attached to this instance and the error appears in its logs — the order can be cancelled until applied.
proxyPage.coverageRightsNote: You can only act on sites you administer: others appear locked.

switchProfilesPage.title: Switch profiles
switchProfilesPage.subtitle: rules that produce port configuration — one profile serves 48-port and 8-port switches
switchProfilesPage.rulesOrderHelp1: Like an access list: write exceptions at the top and catch-all at the bottom.
switchProfilesPage.rulesOrderHelp2: A port gets one rule's config; ports no rule matches stay unchanged.
switchProfilesPage.rulesFirstWins: Rules — the FIRST matching a port wins
switchProfilesPage.previewHelp: Hover a rule to highlight ports it won. Per-port list shows rule and resulting setting.
switchProfilesPage.nothingUntilApply: Nothing is written until you press Apply.
switchProfilesPage.noPortsKnown: No ports known on this device: facade is empty.
switchProfilesPage.uncoveredPorts: {{count}} port(s) no rule matches: left as-is.
switchProfilesPage.noVlansTrunkWarning: No VLAN declared: a full-trunk will deploy nothing until the site plan has VLANs.
switchProfilesPage.readOnly: Read-only — profile definition is reserved for engineer mode.
switchProfilesPage.noProfiles: No switch profile on this site.
switchProfilesPage.selectForPreview: Select a profile to preview its effect on a device.
switchProfilesPage.tagHelp: Devices that carry this tag receive this profile (port intents are written, then pushed with the usual management-VLAN safety checks). Leave empty to enroll only via one-shot preview apply.
switchProfilesPage.enrollViaTag: Enrollment is by tag: put the profile’s tag on a device to apply it. Preview below writes nothing until you use Apply once.
switchProfilesPage.applyOnceHint: Draft test — applies to this preview device only; does not require the enrollment tag.
switchProfilesPage.noFacadePorts: No ports known on this device: facade is empty.

switchDetailPage.snmpReprovisionToast: Supervision was down — re-pushing SNMP to the device in the background…
switchDetailPage.deviceDriftToast: Drift detected: device was changed outside meshcraft
switchDetailPage.configPendingToast: meshcraft configuration not yet applied to device
switchDetailPage.configAppliedVerifiedToast: Configuration applied and verified on device
switchDetailPage.collectorSnmpToast: « {{name}} » now polls this device via SNMP
switchDetailPage.collectorCoverageToast: Collection restored to coverage: any proxy covering this site polls this device
switchDetailPage.defaultMgmtUnreachable: This device's management address is not on the site addressing plan yet.
switchDetailPage.verifyMigrationTitle: Reconfigure management as it's planned on this site
switchDetailPage.noLongerWatchedTitle: This device is no longer monitored
switchDetailPage.watchExcludedNote: Its state will not be reported while its address stays ambiguous. Declare the device's address domain below, or attach scan ranges to distinct domains.
switchDetailPage.noSnmpCollectorTitle: No proxy polls this device via SNMP anymore
switchDetailPage.collectorStrandedNote1: It is attached to proxy « {{name}} », which no longer covers its site. Attachment grants no coverage: the device is collected by no proxy — not that one, which does not see it, nor those covering the site, which are not designated. Its traps have no recipient.
switchDetailPage.collectorStrandedNote2: It is still pinged: its status stays accurate, only collection stopped. Choose a covering collector below, or detach to restore coverage — or add this site to the proxy's coverage from its page.
switchDetailPage.selectionHelp1: Click a port on the facade to configure it in the right panel.
switchDetailPage.selectionHelpCtrl: Ctrl/⌘ click adds or removes a port.
switchDetailPage.selectionHelpShiftCtrl: ⇧+Ctrl/⌘ click adds a range to the selection.
switchDetailPage.selectionHelpMulti: A multi-selection is configured as one block: the panel then shows what differs between ports rather than the first port's value.
switchDetailPage.stpModeTitle: Protocol mode this platform can run. Apply writes it on the device.
switchDetailPage.stpApplyTitle: Write spanning-tree mode on this device
switchDetailPage.stpNotWritable: This platform does not declare spanning-tree as writable.
switchDetailPage.stpReadOnly: Read-only on this site — site engineer rights required to change mode.
switchDetailPage.networkHelp1: The network is the address domain: the space where this IP designates one machine and only one.
switchDetailPage.networkHelp2: Useful when two proxies see the same private range (e.g. 192.168.1.0/24): same network → one device; distinct networks → two devices. On a single-network instance this row stays hidden.
switchDetailPage.networkTitle: The network where this device's address makes sense. It decides which proxy may legitimately monitor it.
switchDetailPage.addressHelp1: This is the IP meshcraft uses to reach the device (ping, SNMP, apply, re-read). It is not the DHCP/static decision — that lives under « Management network ».
switchDetailPage.addressHelp2: Edit it when you changed the address by hand on the switch, at adoption, or during renumbering — otherwise meshcraft keeps talking to the old IP.
switchDetailPage.addressHelp3: When meshcraft itself applies addressing, it updates this field automatically.
switchDetailPage.collectorHelp1: The reference proxy that polls this device via SNMP and should receive its traps.
switchDetailPage.collectorHelp2: With no collector chosen, any proxy covering the site may collect. With several covering proxies, this picks which one does it. Only proxies covering this site can be designated.
switchDetailPage.collectorSelectTitle: The proxy that polls this device via SNMP and receives its traps. With no designated collector, any proxy covering the site handles it. Only proxies covering this site may be designated.
switchDetailPage.monitoringGapsTitleMany: {{count}} monitoring metrics are not exposed by this platform
switchDetailPage.monitoringGapsTitleOne: One monitoring metric is not exposed by this platform
switchDetailPage.monitoringGapsHelp1: This is not delayed collection: the device does not publish these values. No meshcraft version will make them appear here.
switchDetailPage.monitoringGapsHelp2: This list only documents absences for this model. A metric missing on screen without being listed may still be uncollected or unverified on this hardware.
switchDetailPage.absenceObservedTitle: Verified on hardware of this product line
switchDetailPage.absenceAssumedTitle: Inferred from product-line documentation, not verified on hardware
switchDetailPage.absenceAssumedWarning: No one has verified this on hardware yet: another model in the line, or newer firmware, may disprove it. If you observe the opposite, update the connector declaration.
switchDetailPage.tagsHelp1: Tagging does not touch the device. However, a site credential may target a tag: the device then falls under that expected password until an explicit push.
switchDetailPage.tagsHelpTechnical: Technical tags are placed by meshcraft from what this platform's connector declares, and are not removable. They decide credentials the device receives: snmpv3-… for supervision identity, pwpolicy-… for admin password when the platform policy rejects the site secret. They survive rule re-evaluation; matching credentials appear under Configuration → Credentials.
switchDetailPage.tagsHelpRule: Dotted tags are inferred from a site rule: removing them here only lasts until the next re-evaluation. To remove them permanently, change the rule (Tags page).
switchDetailPage.tagAppliedToast: Tag « {{tag}} » applied — nothing was changed on the device
switchDetailPage.tagRemovedRuleToast: « {{tag}} » removed — a site rule will reapply it on next re-evaluation
switchDetailPage.noTrafficNote: No traffic measurements on this port. Interface counters come from SNMP collection: without a designated collector or responding agent, there is nothing to chart — not the same as an idle port.
switchDetailPage.unreachableConfigNote: Switch unreachable — configuration unavailable. Last known state shown.
switchDetailPage.engineerProfilesNote: Profiles defined by the network engineer. Greyed entries are engineer-only.
switchDetailPage.taggedMembersHelpLabel: Help — tagged members on a selection
switchDetailPage.taggedMembersHelp: On a selection, only full replacement makes sense: per-port tagged members are set by selecting a single port.
switchDetailPage.offMgmtPlan: Not on the site management plan
switchDetailPage.tagAppliedProfileBlockedToast: Tag « {{tag}} » kept, but profile « {{profile}} » could not apply: {{reason}}

telemetry.title: Telemetry
telemetry.noMeasurements: No measurements in this window. This device is not collected — no designated collector, silent SNMP agent, or broken proxy tunnel. This is not zero: it is missing data.
telemetry.noSeriesReason: No series arrived for this metric, and the connector does not say whether the platform publishes it.
telemetry.poeBudgetSub: out = delivered to ports · in = declared budget

spanningTreePage.title: Spanning-Tree
spanningTreePage.help: On apply, each device receives the first preferred mode its driver advertises. Select a mode then Add (or double-click). STP is often already in Preferred by default — Drop it first if you need to move it.
spanningTreePage.emptyPreferred: (none — double-click a mode in Available to add)
spanningTreePage.readOnly: Read-only on this site — site admin rights required to change the preference.

unavailable.cpu: This platform does not publish CPU load. Chip temperature is the available load signal where present. No meshcraft version will change that.
unavailable.memory: This platform does not publish memory usage. The firmware does not expose total or free memory.
unavailable.lldp: This platform does not speak LLDP. Neighborhood cannot be drawn from this device; map links from neighbors that do speak LLDP, or change hardware.
unavailable.poe: This model has no PoE hardware to measure: there is no power, current, or budget to track.
unavailable.optical_power: This product line does not expose transceiver optical power. Tracking an optical budget requires hardware that publishes these sensors.

console.clipboardDenied: The browser refused access to the clipboard.
console.frameHint: Many switches refuse to be framed (X-Frame-Options), and a refused frame renders blank without saying so. Opening in a new tab always works; try framing only if you prefer it in place.
console.loading: Asking the controller what this device offers…
console.noAccess: This device offers neither an SSH console nor a web interface meshcraft can reach.
console.openTitle: Open an interactive console on this device
console.socksNeeded: Your browser reaches {{url}} through the meshcraft SOCKS proxy — configure it first, or the page will not load. Nothing is rewritten in transit: this is the device's own interface, at its own address.
console.socksOnce: Copy it now — it is shown once and never again. Regenerating replaces it, which is also how you revoke it.
console.title: Console
console.transportError: The connection to the controller was lost.
console.webOnly: This platform ({{connector}}) has no SSH server: its web interface is the only way to configure it. meshcraft relays it through the site proxy — the login still has to be typed.
